name: Reasoning and answering each step of a request
vision_statement: Every step of a person's request acts on everything the request has established so far, so a reply rests on the work done for it and the person can follow that work, at the cost of the fast tier.
opportunities: The loop's prompt can be rebuilt for each step from a template, cached head and context layers, the newest observations in full and older ones in one line, so a step's input stays small while the final answer still sees everything. That opens questions the parent solution does not ask: how much of the earlier steps a planner must see to keep continuity (from the second step the selected arm replaces the transcript with a short note that refers to step one, and its continuity is unmeasured), how a person is kept informed while a turn works (a first line, interim replies, the trail of what was done) without paying a model call for every line, and how a request that worked before skips the loop by replaying its known steps.
solution_coherence: reason-and-answer lets one step of a request build on the steps before it, and its rebuilt_per_step arm is made of the parts of one step. assemble-a-prompt writes the prompt a step sends within a size budget. choose-a-model-tier picks the model tier a step starts on. answer-a-turn turns the step's decision into the reply to a chat message, opening with a first line from narrate-a-turn and, when the person asks for it, closing with explain-an-answer once the answer is out. replay-known-operations answers a request that worked before by replaying its known steps. core-ml-tasks classifies the message a step is about. answer-end-to-end proves that a message is handled right across the whole path. reply-in-steps decides when a turn that is not finished sends an interim message and what that message holds. show-the-ais-work lays out the trail of the work through show-progress, which streams each event at the level the person wants.
